headline: 2368 Ridge Trail's contract fell through and it is back on market at $559,000 — the tours this board had written off as burned are now your warmest prospect list, and the agent whose buyer said "too high, doesn't like the EIFS" still thinks the house is gone.

hotSignals.signal: 🔥 THE STORY ON THIS HOUSE INVERTED THIS MORNING — AND IN YOUR FAVOR. For ten days every board carried it as 'sold, MLS wrongly reads ACTIVE' and counted the week's buyer tours as wasted. The MLS was never wrong: the contract fell through and the house is genuinely available again at $559,000. The receipt is Gene's own 7:38 AM email to two of those co-op agents, verbatim: "It had been spoken for, that contract has fallen through, and it is back on the market at $559,000. If your buyer liked it, this is a genuine second look — and right now there's no line behind you." FOUR agents walked buyers through in the last eight days — 7/19, two on 7/24, one on 7/25 — three of them inside 26 hours, all of them believing the house was already gone.
hotSignals.action: Two of the four were caught this morning by email — do NOT send them a second one. The one who still thinks it is gone is Cissy S. (RealtySouth-OTM-Acton Rd), and she gets a CALL, not an email, because her Saturday read is the one worth reopening: "too high" with the stated reason "doesn't like the EIFS." Put the EIFS on the table yourself rather than letting it quietly kill a second look. That same call does a second job — she asked about 5167 Lake Crest on 7/22 and withdrew when told it was under contract, and nobody has ever offered her a backup position. ⚠️ Do not reach for a price cut on this: the price case is genuinely mixed — the 7/19 agent said "JUST RIGHT" and lost on schools and yard size. Find out what actually killed the contract first; if the appraisal came in short that is a data answer, not an anecdote. ⚠️ Quote $559,000 only — $545,000 was the dead contract's estimated close and must never be published. ⚠️ The 7/24 pair still owe reads.

hotSignals.signal: ✅ CLOSED OUT BEFORE NOON — the counter is delivered and the gap is halved. Sequence, fully receipted: the buyers countered back at 7:59 PM Sunday from a restaurant, 59 minutes PAST the expiry their own written offer set; Gene texted buyer's agent Cassie C. (RE/MAX Advantage) at 5:41 AM "will get you a response this am"; called his seller at 9:15; at 9:32 the seller ruled it — "Counter at $295k with $7k. But we keep the washer and dryer downstairs" — and at 10:30 Gene delivered it to Cassie with the appliance clarification and the note that additional interest makes further movement unlikely. Effective position $288,000. The gap went from $12,000 to $6,000, and the 5:41 promise was kept ninety minutes early.
hotSignals.action: The number is settled; the exposure is now paperwork. TWO asks, both today. First, their pre-approval letter is papered at exactly $280,000 — below even their own previous counter, let alone the number now in front of them. Nobody has asked for a refreshed one. Ask now so the lender's re-paper runs in parallel instead of adding days at the back; that, not the spread, is the actual risk on this deal. Second, everything from the original offer forward has lived in text messages — the moment she says yes it needs to be a signed counter, not a thumbs-up. ⚠️ Still unanswered since 7/16: whether the ARC Realty offer is alive. If it is, your seller is choosing between two offers rather than waiting on one.

hotSignals.signal: ⭐ THE THING THAT HAS BLOCKED THIS RE-OFFER FOR TWO WEEKS MOVES TODAY. The buyers behind Kenneth R.'s conditional re-offer are listing their own Sterrett house TODAY (his SMS Sunday 5:16 PM) — that house not being under contract is the entire reason the re-offer has had no legs. ✅ Two other items on this file closed themselves this morning: the seller's eight-day silence ended at 8:17 with a full weekly report carrying 883 Zillow views and 45 saves, and the 7/23 showing agent finally answered the nudge at 8:22.
hotSignals.action: Rebook with Quin W. (EXIT Realty Southern Select) — Sunday's 3:00 showing, number eleven on this house, cancelled at 11:44 because the buyer got called into work. That is a scheduling problem, not a lost buyer, and the co-op agent's number is on the notice. Then use today's real lever with Kenneth R.: their house going live is the day to ask for movement, because until it is under contract the re-offer is a wish. The 96-hour bar passed Sunday with the same answer as the 48- and 72-hour bars. ⚠️ Fold William K.'s foundation-and-concrete objection into your seller conversation — it is nameable and specific, which makes it workable.

hotSignals.signal: 🟡 THE 10:30 IS BEHIND YOU. The second inspection — booked Sunday 3:18 PM by buyer's agent Manda L. (ARC Realty Vestavia) with the showing remark reading verbatim "Meeting hvac company" — ran 10:30 to 11:30 this morning. ✅ And the seller was not left in the dark: a portfolio report reached him at 8:18 AM carrying this file at $899,000, under contract, closing 8/14. ⚠️ NOT ASSERTED, and it still matters: that anything is wrong with the HVAC, what a contractor found, what it would cost, or that any of it threatens the close. Friday's repair request has still never arrived, so this remains the only hard signal of what the buyers are chasing.
hotSignals.action: The useful question now is what the contractor actually found — ask Manda L. rather than waiting for a repair request that is already late. Same call, give her the thing that has been asked five times: a weekday DATE the sellers meet the city, not "next week." The buyer side opened Saturday with "I know we are on a time limit," the buyers are described as very concerned, and nothing has gone to them in writing — a date, even an imperfect one, converts worry into a timeline. Send the permit question to your coordinator that has been an unsent draft since Saturday 10:44 AM; it is the cheapest item on this file. ⚠️ The 7/24 certificate-of-completion visit NEVER HAPPENED — the inspector left without conducting it. And the written "interested: Yes" backup buyer, Kulsum B. (Keller Williams Hoover), is eight days uncalled.
